articles.title: Apple's Siri AI launches September 9 with waitlist and complete EU block due to DMA
articles.description: Apple's rebuilt Gemini-powered Siri AI arrives on iOS 27 waitlisted and English-only, with the EU completely blocked over Digital Markets Act requirements for third-party assistant access.
articles.content: Apple confirmed the EU block stems from DMA rules requiring equal device access for rival voice assistants. Apple proposed a Trusted System Agent architecture as an alternative, but the European Commission rejected it. Approximately 450 million iPhone and iPad users in the EU are affected, with no timeline for availability. Siri AI also faces regulatory delays in China.

articles.title: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash Cyber for agentic workflows and cybersecurity
articles.description: Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash with improvements in coding and agentic tasks, alongside Flash Cyber for vulnerability detection and automated patching available to trusted defenders.

Flash Cyber is available through Google's new Fairwind Program for trusted defenders, reflecting growing concerns about AI-powered cyber threats.

articles.description: Tether AI Research launched open-source translation models that run privately and offline on everyday devices, covering 19 African languages alongside European language pairs.

The models are available in 800M and 2B parameter versions. The release supports European languages relevant to multicultural EU communities and aligns with EU AI Act requirements for transparent and accessible AI systems.

articles.title: TSMC says Europe's chip strategy is shifting from factory construction to demand creation
articles.description: TSMC reports that Europe's semiconductor push is moving beyond factory building toward demand development, design support, and talent building across the continent.
articles.content: The assessment comes as TSMC's Dresden fab in Saxony progresses toward production. The shift signals maturity in Europe's chip strategy: having secured manufacturing capacity through the Chips Act, attention now turns to building the design ecosystem and skilled workforce needed for self-sustaining semiconductor innovation rather than import-dependent fabs.

articles.title: Germany's Uplift Ventures debuts EUR100 million fund to bridge Europe's DeepTech financing gap
articles.description: Uplift Ventures launched its inaugural EUR100 million venture capital fund to back European deep tech companies from Seed to Series A, targeting one of the largest financing gaps in the European tech ecosystem.
articles.content: The Hamburg- and Berlin-based venture platform aims to close the funding gap between seed and growth stages for European DeepTech startups. The fund will invest in high-growth technology companies and select deep-tech venture capital funds across Europe, focusing on areas including AI, robotics, and advanced manufacturing. The launch comes amid record European AI investment, with startups capturing 55% of all VC capital in H1 2026.

articles.title: European Commission begins AI Act enforcement against 30+ companies and discusses cyber risks with OpenAI and Anthropic
articles.description: The European Commission has sent Requests for Information to over 30 AI companies, marking the first enforcement actions under the AI Act. Brussels confirmed recent exchanges with OpenAI and Anthropic about cybersecurity risks.
articles.content: The Commission's RFIs cover two areas: safety and security of AI systems including general-purpose models, and copyright and transparency obligations. The Commission has not disclosed which companies received the requests but confirmed direct discussions with OpenAI and Anthropic about cyber risks. ENISA continues bilateral onboarding discussions with companies to establish security standards for advanced model access.

articles.title: US urges hands-off AI regulation at G20 while EU pushes comprehensive rules
articles.description: The United States pressed G20 members to take a light-touch approach to AI regulation, while Elon Musk slammed EU tech rules as inhibiting innovation. The EU continues to push its comprehensive AI Act framework.
articles.content: At the G20 tech ministerial in Chapel Hill, the US called for deregulation emphasizing industry growth over regulatory constraints. Musk criticized the EU's regulatory approach and defended AI data centre construction. The divide highlights the growing transatlantic gap on AI governance, with the EU maintaining its first-mover regulatory framework while the US favours innovation-first policies.

articles.title: OpenAI's Astra becomes first model to cross Critical cybersecurity capability threshold
articles.description: OpenAI says its upcoming Astra model can find and exploit previously unknown security flaws without human guidance, meeting the Critical threshold under its Preparedness Framework.
articles.content: Astra achieved a perfect score on ExploitBench and discovered two zero-day vulnerabilities during evaluation. The model can build full browser-compromise chains and local privilege-escalation chains against hardened systems. OpenAI is implementing stronger safeguards including improved refusal training and access controls, with advanced cybersecurity capabilities initially available to a limited group of testers through Daybreak Blue.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with improved coding and cybersecurity
articles.description: Anthropic released updated Claude models with 75% cheaper cache reads and improved coding performance. Mythos 5.1 includes gated access via export controls, while Fable 5.1 is generally available.
articles.content: The models arrive three months after the Fable 5 line shipped in June. Fable 5.1 can now discover software vulnerabilities but is restricted from developing exploits. Mythos 5.1 has stronger capabilities and remains behind restricted access. Both models feature anti-distillation mechanisms and improved alignment. The launch comes as the European Commission confirms discussions with Anthropic about cybersecurity risks of its models.

articles.title: EU Cyber Resilience Act reporting deadline arrives September 11 with ENISA's filing portal
articles.description: Starting September 11, 2026, manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform under the EU Cyber Resilience Act.
articles.content: The CRA introduces mandatory vulnerability and incident reporting for products with digital elements in the EU Digital Single Market. ENISA's Single Reporting Platform launches the same day reporting becomes mandatory. Manufacturers, importers, and distributors must notify ENISA and national CSIRTs within 24 hours of discovering actively exploited vulnerabilities. Non-compliance can carry fines up to 15 million euros or 3% of turnover.

articles.title: EuroHPC signs EUR387.8M contract for LUMI-AI supercomputer in Finland
articles.description: EuroHPC JU awarded French vendor Bull a EUR387.8 million contract to deploy LUMI-AI in Kajaani, the sixth AI Factory machine, aiming for a tenfold rise in AI capacity versus current LUMI.
articles.content: The system will sit at CSC Kajaani data centre and serve the LUMI AI Factory consortium of Finland, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Norway and Poland. It will use AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th-gen EPYC CPUs, with installation planned for the second half of 2027. EuroHPC and the consortium split the cost 50/50. Aimed first at European startups and SMEs.
